chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Zayd, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The private part (is made permissible/halal) by three: marriage by inheritance, marriage without inheritance, and marriage by possession of the right (concubinage).'

key_terms.الْفَرْجُ: The private part (of a woman), referring to sexual permissibility

ai.seo_question: What are the three ways a woman's private part becomes permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the three canonical modes of sexual permissibility, categorizing them into permanent marriage (nikah) and temporary possession (milk al-yamin). This classification reflects the foundational Shia jurisprudence distinguishing between the enduring marital bond, which includes inheritance rights, and the concubinage relationship, which was prevalent in early Islamic society. The hadith serves as a primary textual basis for understanding the scope of mahram and non-mahram interactions within the framework of fiqh al-jafari.
